newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's coffee sees cloudy, rainy weekend weather.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's coffee sees cloudy, rainy weekend weather.

text.p: Brazil's coffee regions saw cloudy weather and much rain over the weekend with minimum temperatures holding above 10 degrees Celsius, private weather service Somar Meteorologia said Sunday.

The forecast for early Monday morning was for minimum temperatures of around 10 degrees in north Parana and around eight degrees in high regions in the south of Minas Gerais state such as Pocos de Caldas, said Somar forecaster Marcos Massari.
"But temperatures will not fall below eight degrees," Massari said.

A polar air mass which has caused frosts in the far south of the country was now moving out to the ocean and frosts were only predicted in the most southern state of Rio Grande do Sul early Monday morning, said Manoel Rangel of the National Institute of Meteorology.
A second polar mass which was due to arrive Monday in the south of the country was coming in from the sea and would therefore be bringing humidity, posing no frost threat.
"The cloudy weather will continue in the coffee regions. The coldest weather will not be in the coffee areas but along the east by the coast," Massari said.
Rain was forecast to continue in the coffee regions, particularly in the north of Sao Paulo state and south of Minas Gerais, until May 29, he added.
The next polar air mass expected to arrive in Rio Grande do Sul on May 29 was likely to be even more humid and therefore also posed no frost threat, Massari said.
